page.layout: One page of running text. A marginal note "Augustinus." stands in the left margin beside the paragraph beginning "De talibus". The page number is at the head, centred. The catchword "que" stands alone at the bottom right.

main_text.p: » in parabolis: quas explicabat feorsim discipu- » lis. Matth.13.v.10. His enim datum erat, » nosse mysteria regni cælorum: illis non item.v. II.&c.

Augusti-nus.De talibus quoque intelligendum esse Augustinum, in postremis scriptis, oftenderem passim; si, praeter verba, etiam loca allegâsset Grotius. Inquit ille, lib. de correp. & grat.c.8. Mirandum est quidem, multumq; mirandum; quòd filiis suis quibusdam, (Nota, quibusdam. Nimirum ita illi filii dicuntur: quemadmodum discipuli dicebātur nobis; at non esse verè Deo, nisi secundum vocationem auditumque externum, ibid.c.9. ipsimet abitu suo ostendebant) quos regeneravit in Christo, (per Baptismum externum, lavacrum regenerationis) quibus fidem, spem, dilectionem dedit; non dat perseveran- stiam[?]. Pergendum autem erat: Cùm filiis alienis tanta scelera dimittat, atque impertitâ gratiâ suâ, faciat filios suos; putâ re-cipiendo in gremium Ecclesiæ per Ba-ptismum. Ita enim addit: Sed etiam illud non minùs mirum est; & tamen verum est, at-

page.notes: The first line of the page continues the quotation from the previous page; the » marks at the start of the lines are printed marks, copied as they stand. "II.&c." is read from a small numeral and may be "11.&c.". The last word of the paragraph is printed "perseveran-" with "stiam" on the next line; the last glyphs are unclear and are marked [?]. The printed "Inquitille" is read as "Inquit ille".
